'''''Solanum umbelliferum'' var. ''xanti''''', known commonly as '''chaparral nightshade''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SOXA|taxon=Solanum xanti|accessdate=17 November 2015}}</ref> '''purple nightshade''', and '''San Diego nightshade''', is a variety of [[nightshade]]. It is native to the [[western United States]] in [[Arizona]], [[California]], [[Nevada]], and [[Oregon]], and to north-western Mexico in [[Baja California]].<ref name="jepson">[http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?7625,7682,7701 Jepson] . accessed 1.27.2013</ref>

The plant grows in [[chaparral]], [[California oak woodland|oak woodland]]s, conifer forests, desert [[Madrean Sky Islands]], and other [[habitat]]s.<ref>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=7666 Calflora database: ''Solanum xanti'']. accessed 1.27.2013</ref>

==Description==
''Solanum umbelliferum'' var. ''xanti'' grows as a perennial herb or [[shrub|subshrub]] producing a branching hairy stem up to about {{convert|90|cm|in}} in maximum height. The leaves are up to 7 centimeters long and are lance-shaped to oval, mostly unlobed except for occasional lobes at the bases of the blades.

It flowers from February to June in the wild, bearing an [[umbel]]-shaped [[inflorescence]] with many purple-blue flowers up to 3 centimeters wide. The fruit is a green [[Berry (botany)|berry]] 1 to 1.5 centimeters wide.<ref name="jepson"/>

==Cultivation==
The plant is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] by specialty [[plant nursery|plant nurseries]] for planting in perennial border, [[xeriscaping|drought-tolerant]] and [[native plant]] gardens. It grows from sunny locations to dry shade, such as under native oaks.<ref>[http://www.cnplx.info/nplx/species?taxon=Solanum+xanti CNPLX—California Native Plant Link Exchange: ''Solanum xanti'' — Nursery and Seed Sources] . accessed 1.27.2013</ref><ref>[http://www.laspilitas.com/nature-of-california/plants/solanum-xanti Las Pilitas Nursery: ''Solanum xanti'' — horticulture] . accessed 1.27.2013</ref><ref>[http://www.smgrowers.com/products/plants/plantdisplay.asp?plant_id=3544 San Marcos Growers: ''Solanum xanti''] . accessed 1.27.2013</ref>

The plant is deer resistant, due to its toxic qualities.
In common with many other members in the Solanaceace family, all parts of the plant are toxic, especially the unripe fruit. Toxicity is from Solanine and glycol-alkaloids, chaconine, and solasodine. There is no antidote for ''Solanum'' poisoning. Symptoms include:
* Cardiovascular system (tachycardia, arrhythmia, and hypotension)
* Central nervous system (delirium, psychomotor, agitation, paralysis, coma, and convulsion)
* Gastrointestinal tract (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://edenbythebay.blogspot.com/2013/10/poison-gardens-purple-nightshade.html|title=Eden by the Bay: Poison Gardens – Purple Nightshade|date=23 October 2013}}</ref>
